analysis.cluster: Crew, seats, handling, mounts and death
analysis.summary: Two fields in this group fall below 80%. armament.seat (66.7%) is a measuring artefact: the schema says the seat defaults to driver but never says whether to write that default, so some coders wrote it and others left it out. on_death.outcomes (72.2%) splits because 'respawn' is worded for a shooter, nothing says which basis an RTS unit that simply dies should get, and decision 3C's default is not written into the word lists; all 12 reports hesitated on it. Against the samples, all three coders made the Hammer a two-seat tank because its background text mentions a gunner, and gave it a slow turret. The sample is right on the crew (the source fires one weapon at a time from one turret, and background text should not add seats) but wrong on the mount (a large tank's main turret should be slow-turret), so the sample needs a fix. I propose these changes: leave out seat 'driver' and check that every seat exists on the unit; drop the 'lore' crew basis and give an RTS unit a second seat only when it fires two weapons at once; code an RTS unit that simply dies as a proposal using the 3C default; pick the mount with an ordered test based on the physical mount; keep the mobility type's default handling unless a listed reason applies; and sharpen the solo-fallback terms. Smaller fixes cover death notes, empty trait lists and boost versus retreat.

proposals.evidence: armament.seat agreement 66.7% (below the threshold; all three coders agree on only 3 of 6 units). Coriflemen: A (none), B (none), C driver. Terror Drone: A driver, B (none), C driver. Siege Tank: A driver, B (none), C driver. Against the reference: 27.8%. The samples leave the seat out on every driver weapon, but all three coders wrote driver on the IFV missiles. All three also gave the Hammer a 'gunner' seat (see crew-model-rts). Hesitations: 1 report (C-ra3: Hammer gunner or driver). The 3 Battlefield reports flagged unclear rules on seat versus slot (see seat-and-primary).
proposals.root_cause: schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs weapon.seat (and ability.seat) says only 'Default: driver'. It never says whether to write the default, so B left it out and A and C wrote it (A only on some units). The seat-roles term driver ('In a solo unit also aims, fires and uses abilities') reads like an invitation to write it on solo units. scripts/agreement.mjs compares raw values, so a missing seat and 'driver' count as a disagreement although they mean the same thing. Nothing checks that a seat exists on the unit, so a solo unit can carry a 'gunner' weapon.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs weapon.properties.seat.description and $defs ability.properties.seat.description (docs/fields.md regenerated); data/vocab/seat-roles.json term driver (new source_rule); scripts/validate.mjs unit checks; scripts/agreement.mjs armament.seat reader
proposals.change:
weapon.seat description, new text: "Proposal (copied from the source when crew.basis is in-game). Which seat fires it. Leave it out when the driver fires it. That covers every weapon of a solo, squad or remote unit and the driver's own weapons in a multi-seat unit. Write it only for another seat the unit has: gunner or commander when the crew model or crew.seats has that seat, or a passenger seat when it matches crew.passengers.kind."
ability.seat description, new text: "Proposal (copied from the source when crew.basis is in-game). Which seat triggers it. Leave it out when the driver does. A passive ability has no seat. Write it only for another seat the unit has, as for weapons."
seat-roles.json driver, new source_rule: "Never written on a source unit. A weapon or ability with no seat belongs to the driver."
validate.mjs, two new errors on source units: (1) "seat 'driver' is the default; leave it out"; (2) "seat '<x>' is not a seat of this unit", where the allowed seats are crew-models[model].seats, plus crew.seats[].role, plus crew.passengers.kind.
agreement.mjs: read a missing seat as driver.
proposals.expected: Riflemen: no seat on any weapon for all three (C drops 'driver'). Terror Drone and Siege Tank: no seat (A and C drop 'driver'). IFV: the missiles have no seat (all three drop 'driver'). The passenger weapons keep passenger-module, which is valid because crew.passengers.kind is passenger-module. Attack helicopter: the pilot weapons and countermeasures have no seat, and the cannon and gunner missiles keep gunner, which is valid for driver-gunner. Hammer: no seat (solo under crew-model-rts). The coders' 'gunner' on the stolen weapon becomes an error. armament.seat reaches 100% on the pilot units and matches the published samples, which need no change.
proposals.side_effects: docs/fields.md regenerates. tests/validate.test.mjs needs cases for the two new errors. Concept cards are untouched: parts.*.seat stays required there, so the generator still writes 'driver' explicitly. The rule codes no unit in the 28 games badly. A unit whose driver has no gun (a Foxhole light tank) simply has no weapon without a seat.

proposals.evidence: main weapon.family is 77.8% (below the threshold). On the attack helicopter, A and B have rockets and C has autocannon, because C put the gunner's chin cannon in the primary slot with seat gunner. B made the pilot's rockets primary, and A had no primary at all, only options. Three reports hesitated on slot versus seat on a two-seat unit (A-, B- and C-battlefield). Unclear rules in A-bf, B-bf and C-bf all say that primary and secondary are set for the whole unit while each seat has its own main gun.
proposals.root_cause: Seat is per weapon and slot is per unit, and no rule links them. Decision 2A (the buyer drives and fires the main weapon) is not written into either field. The schema also marks seat as a pure proposal, yet for shooter vehicles the coders, rightly, copied the source's seats, so it is unclear whether 2A or the source decides.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs weapon.properties.seat.description (together with seat-leave-out-driver) and weapon.properties.slot.description; scripts/validate.mjs. Cross-group: armament.slot belongs to the armament group, and this rule is forced by decision 2A and the seat field.
proposals.change:
Add to the seat description: "When crew.basis is in-game, write the seat that fires it in the source. When crew.basis is a proposal, follow decision 2A: the driver fires the main weapon, and only a second weapon that the source fires at the same time goes to the gunner."
Add to the slot description: "primary is the driver's main weapon. A second seat's own main gun is secondary. A gunner's weapon is primary only when the driver has no weapon in the source."
validate.mjs, new error: a weapon with slot primary and a seat other than driver, on a unit where some weapon has no seat (so the driver has one).
proposals.expected: Attack helicopter: the pilot's rocket pods are primary with no seat, and the chin cannon is secondary with seat gunner, for all three. C moves the cannon from primary to secondary. The main weapon becomes rockets for all three, which settles the helicopter half of main weapon.family. Whether a loadout's default option counts as primary (A's case) is for the armament group. IFV: the missiles are primary for the driver, as the sample has. All other pilot units are single-seat and unchanged.
proposals.side_effects: The armament group must accept that primary means the driver's main weapon. Their option-group rule (is the default option primary?) still decides A's helicopter. The x-provenance marker on seat should read 'per crew.basis' rather than always 'proposal', and agreement.mjs should mark armament.seat as partly proposal. Scope: a Foxhole light tank (the driver only drives) gets the gunner's main gun as primary, which is correct. A PlanetSide 2 Liberator gets the pilot's nose gun as primary, and its notes should say that the belly gun is the heavy weapon.

proposals.evidence: crew.model is 100% among coders but contradicts the sample. All three made the Hammer driver-gunner, basis lore, solo_fallback full-control, where the sample has solo, basis proposal, no fallback (crew.model and solo_fallback both 66.7% against the reference). 6 of 12 reports hesitated on crew model or basis: A-ra3 (Hammer lore or solo; Drone solo or remote; IFV basis), A-sc2 (Siege Tank solo or driver-gunner, voice lines), B-ra3 (Hammer; IFV mixed basis; Drone remote), B-sc2 (do voice lines count as lore?), C-ra3 (Hammer; Drone remote; IFV mixed basis), C-sc2 (commander seat). Unclear rules: A-ra3 (no basis for uncrewed robots), A-sc2 and B-sc2 (voice lines), B-ra3 and C-ra3 (an in-game passenger seat next to a driver who exists only in lore; whether lore forces a multi-seat model).
proposals.root_cause: crew.basis offers 'lore = the source describes a crew', so any background text that names a gunner becomes a reason to add a gunner seat. Almost every RTS tank has such text or crew voice lines, so the lists would turn most tanks into two-seaters on flavour text rather than on what the unit does. Nothing says when a unit that the source moves as one piece should get a second seat, when an uncrewed machine counts as remote, or which basis covers an in-game passenger seat next to an invented driver. The Soviet flavour (faction-flavours.json) favours driver-gunner, which pulls the same way for the Hammer. The source is clear: the Hammer can fire only one weapon at a time, and its stolen weapon is mounted on the side of the same turret.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json crew.properties.basis (enum and description) and crew.properties.model.description; data/vocab/crew-models.json: new source_rule on solo, driver-gunner, driver-gunner-commander, squad and remote, plus two tie_breaks
proposals.change:
1. crew.basis enum: ["in-game", "proposal"] (drop "lore"). New description: "in-game = players operate this unit in the source and its seats are copied from there (shooters such as Battlefield, PlanetSide 2, Foxhole, Renegade or MechWarrior), or the source moves a group of soldiers as one unit with one order (a squad). proposal = our pick for a player version. That covers every other unit: every RTS vehicle, aircraft, walker, drone and lone soldier. A crew named only in background text or voice lines changes nothing; mention it in notes. The basis covers the operating seats (model, seats, solo fallback). Passenger seats are always copied from the source."
2. crew.model description: "Who operates the unit. Copy the source's seats when it has them. Otherwise follow the coding rules on Crew models: solo, unless the unit fires two weapons at the same time."
3. source_rule texts:
- solo: "The default for a unit with no player seats in the source. An uncrewed machine is solo unless remote applies. A crew named in lore or voice lines does not change it."
- driver-gunner: "In-game when the source has a driver seat and a gun seat. As a proposal, use it only for a vehicle, walker, hover or aircraft of medium size or bigger that fires two weapons at the same time from separate mounts, such as a main gun plus anti-air missiles or a machine gun that picks its own targets. The driver keeps the main weapon and the gunner gets the other (decision 2A). These do not count: weapons swapped by a mode or toggle, weapons the source fires one at a time, and weapons set by a passenger."
- driver-gunner-commander: "In-game only, when the source has a separate seat that spots, marks or commands. Never proposed for a unit without player seats."
- squad: "In-game when the source moves two or more bodies as one unit for their whole life, with one order and a shared fate (Company of Heroes or Dawn of War squads). Units that come in pairs but then act alone are solo."
- remote: "Only when the source has a person who stays behind, outside the machine, while steering it (a soldier who parks to fly a drone). A note in the lore that the machine was once remote-controlled does not count."
4. tie_breaks on crew-models:
{terms: [solo, driver-gunner], rule: "Count what the source unit does, not what its text says. Two weapons firing at the same time from separate mounts: driver-gunner. Anything else: solo. Faction flavours never decide a source unit's crew; they only weight generated cards."}
{terms: [solo, remote], rule: "Remote only when an operator stays on the field in the source. Otherwise an uncrewed machine is solo."}
proposals.expected: Hammer: solo, proposal, no solo_fallback, for all three, because it fires one weapon at a time and the stolen gun sits on the same turret. That matches the sample, and the coders' lore mention moves to crew.notes. Siege Tank: solo, proposal, for all three (one gun at a time, set by the mode), which settles A-sc2, B-sc2 and C-sc2. Terror Drone: solo, proposal, for all (no operator on the field). IFV: solo, proposal, with 1 passenger seat of kind passenger-module, for all. A and C change lore to proposal, B changes in-game to proposal, and the passenger seat stays a copied fact. Riflemen: squad, in-game, for all. Attack helicopter: driver-gunner, in-game, full-control, for all. The published samples need no change.
proposals.side_effects: Schema enum change: no published sample uses 'lore', so none break, but the pilot files of A, B and C (Hammer, IFV) would fail and need recoding. docs/fields.md and docs/vocabularies.md regenerate. In the 28 games, some RTS units become driver-gunner proposals, which is intended under 2A: Company of Heroes tanks whose machine guns fire alongside the main gun, and anti-air-plus-cannon units such as an RA2 Apocalypse, a CnC3 Mammoth or an SC2 Thor. Risk: SupCom and PA units with many weapons still get only two seats, and no RTS unit is ever proposed a commander seat. Cross-group pointer for the armour group: armour-models crew-casualties bans the squad crew model while citing Company of Heroes soldiers as its example (C-coh1). This rule keeps CoH squads as squad, so the armour list must change, not this one.

proposals.evidence: solo_fallback is 100% (all three gave the attack helicopter full-control), but all 3 Battlefield reports hesitated (A, B and C weighed needs-crew and seat-swap). Two logged a gap (A-bf, C-bf: the driver keeps his own weapons while the gunner's weapons sit idle). Two logged an unclear rule (A-bf: no term for this; C-bf: full-control says 'fire everything' while its own Battlefield example means only the main gun). These are all the reports that coded a real multi-seat unit. The coders' Hammer full-control falls away under crew-model-rts.
proposals.root_cause: full-control's description ('One player can drive and fire everything') contradicts its example ('Battlefield tanks: the driver has the main gun'). needs-crew's description ('A seat's weapon or ability does nothing without a player in it') also fits a gunner's idle cannon. seat-swap partly fits too, since a lone pilot can hop seats. There is no tie-break.
proposals.target: data/vocab/solo-fallback.json: terms full-control, seat-swap and needs-crew (description and examples), plus a new tie_breaks entry
proposals.change:
full-control description: "Alone, the player drives and fires the driver seat's own weapons, including the main weapon (decision 2A). Weapons in other seats either pass to the driver or wait for a teammate; say which in crew notes." Examples: keep the Renegade one, and replace 'Battlefield tanks: the driver has the main gun' with "Battlefield tanks and attack helicopters: the driver keeps the main gun or the rockets, while the second seat's gun waits for a teammate".
seat-swap description: "Alone, the player must change seats to shoot, because the driver seat has no weapon of its own: drive or shoot, not both." Check the PlanetSide 2 Liberator example against the source. If its pilot has a nose gun, it is full-control under this test, so move it there and give seat-swap an example whose driver has no gun.
needs-crew description: "A core job, such as firing or reloading the main gun, cannot be done at all by a lone player, not even by changing seats. Weapons in other seats that only wait for a teammate are full-control, not this."
auto-gunner: unchanged.
tie_breaks: {terms: [full-control, seat-swap, needs-crew, auto-gunner], rule: "Ask what one player alone can do. If the driver seat has a weapon of its own, pick full-control, even when other seats' weapons go quiet. If it has none and the player can change seats to shoot, pick seat-swap. If a core job can't be done alone at all, pick needs-crew. Pick auto-gunner only when the source makes empty gun seats fire by themselves. A proposal crew is always full-control (decision 2A)."}
proposals.expected: Attack helicopter: the pilot has rocket pods and a missile of his own, so full-control for all three with nothing left to weigh. Hammer: no fallback (solo). Any RTS driver-gunner proposal: full-control.
proposals.side_effects: The validator already requires a fallback for multi-seat models, so it needs no change. In the 28-game scope, Foxhole vehicles whose driver has no gun become seat-swap or needs-crew under the test. Check each against the source while researching.

proposals.evidence: on_death.outcomes is 72.2% (below the threshold); 55.6% against the reference. Hammer: A respawn, B bail-out, C respawn. IFV: A respawn, B bail-out, C respawn (the sample has bail-out for both). Attack helicopter: A respawn, B respawn, C respawn plus bail-out. Basis: A and C coded every RTS death as respawn, in-game. B coded the Hammer and IFV as bail-out, proposal, and the others as respawn, in-game. The samples have respawn, proposal (Drone) and bail-out, proposal (Hammer, IFV). Hesitations: 12 of 12 reports (on_death: A-sc2, B-coh1, B-ra3, B-sc2, C-coh1, C-ra3; on_death.basis: A-coh1, A-ra3, B-ra3, C-sc2; on_death.outcomes: A-bf, B-bf, C-bf). Unclear rules in 11 reports (A-coh1, A-ra3, A-sc2, B-bf, B-coh1, B-ra3, B-sc2, C-bf, C-coh1, C-ra3, C-sc2): which basis applies when an RTS unit simply dies, and bail-out versus jumping out by hand.
proposals.root_cause: The term respawn ('the player returns to the buy screen') describes our game, so for an RTS unit that just dies, coders could not tell whether that was an in-game fact or our proposal. Decision 3C's default (bail-out for crewed vehicles, respawn for infantry and drones) appears only in docs/proposal.md, not in the field or the word list. on_death.basis has no description at all. bail-out says the crew 'eject' and does not say whether jumping out by hand before the wreck counts (Battlefield's burning phase), so C added bail-out next to respawn. Answer to the question: the basis for an RTS unit that simply dies is proposal. Lore is not an option for on_death, and the source shows no outcome to call in-game.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json on_death.properties.basis (new description); data/vocab/on-death.json: respawn description, new source_rule on respawn, bail-out, wreck, death-blast and pilot-eject, and two tie_breaks; scripts/validate.mjs
proposals.change:
on_death.basis description: "in-game = the source shows what happens when this unit dies: a wreck or husk others can use, a blast that hurts what is near, crew or a pilot getting out on their own, or, in a game where players come back after dying, the player going back to pick again. proposal = the source shows nothing special, because the unit is simply gone (almost every RTS unit). Then code the default from decision 3C: bail-out for a crewed machine that is not infantry, respawn for everything else. When the source shows an outcome, code only that, with basis in-game, and never add the default."
respawn description: "Nothing is left: the unit is simply gone. In a player version the player goes back to the buy screen (a remote operator goes back to their parked soldier)."
respawn source_rule: "In-game in a game where players come back after their unit dies, including a vehicle whose crew die inside it. For a unit that is simply gone in the source, it is the proposal for infantry, organic units and uncrewed machines."
bail-out source_rule: "In-game when the crew or riders get out on their own as the vehicle dies. Jumping out by hand before it dies does not count; in our game that is the hold-X key every vehicle has. It is the proposal for any crewed machine outside the infantry class that is simply gone in the source. Everyone inside gets out, passengers too."
wreck source_rule: "In-game only when the remains can be repaired, recrewed or salvaged. Remains that only block the way or give cover do not count; put them in notes."
death-blast source_rule: "In-game only when the explosion hurts units nearby. A blast that is only for show does not count."
pilot-eject source_rule: "In-game when the pilot leaves the wreck as a unit that can walk to a new vehicle or a pickup."
tie_breaks:
{terms: [respawn, bail-out], rule: "A crewed vehicle that is simply gone in the source: bail-out, basis proposal. A vehicle in a shooter whose crew die inside it: respawn, basis in-game, even when they could have jumped out by hand first."}
{terms: [respawn, wreck, death-blast, pilot-eject], rule: "Use two outcomes only when the source shows both, such as a husk that also explodes. Never pair a sourced outcome with the 3C default."}
validate.mjs, new error on source units: when basis is proposal, outcomes must be [bail-out] if nature is crewed-machine and class is not infantry, otherwise [respawn]. Message: "a proposal death outcome is the 3C default; if the source shows another outcome, set basis in-game".
proposals.expected: Terror Drone: [respawn], proposal, for all three (all change basis from in-game; matches the sample). Hammer: [bail-out], proposal (A and C change; B and the sample already have it). IFV: [bail-out], proposal (A and C change; B and the sample already have it). Siege Tank: [bail-out], proposal, for all three (all three had respawn, in-game, but the source tank is simply gone and it is a crewed machine). Riflemen: [respawn], proposal, for all three (basis changes; dropped weapons go to notes, see on-death-notes). Attack helicopter: [respawn], in-game, for all three (C drops bail-out, since the crew die if still inside). on_death.outcomes and basis reach 100%, and the samples need no change.
proposals.side_effects: agreement.mjs should also measure on_death.basis. docs/fields.md and docs/vocabularies.md regenerate, and tests need cases for the new validator error. In the 28 games, these become in-game outcomes as intended: CnC3 husks, SupCom and PA wrecks that can be reclaimed, Company of Heroes wrecks that can be salvaged or recrewed, CoH2 US vehicle crews bailing out (research/registry-notes/games-r4.md), Generals veteran pilots walking away from wrecks, and MechWarrior ejection. Gaps that remain: heroes or Necron warriors in Dawn of War that go down and get back up, and the Generals battle bus that becomes a bunker, have no term. Code the nearest term and add a fit_note. Decision 3C lists only five outcomes, so a 'downed, can be revived' term would need Mustafa's approval before the 1.0 freeze.

proposals.evidence: Gaps in 7 of 12 reports. The Terror Drone Surprise protocol can make a dying Soviet vehicle release a drone (A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3, twice in C). The IFV's rider is killed with the car (B-ra3, C-ra3). Riflemen leave special weapons on the ground for anyone to pick up (A-coh1, B-coh1). Battlefield crews can jump out by hand while the vehicle burns (A-bf, B-bf, C-bf). Under on-death-plain-death none of these changes the outcome, but on_death has no place for them, so coders reached for outcome terms instead.
proposals.root_cause: The on_death group has only outcomes and basis. Unlike crew, mobility and sensors, it has no notes field, so a true but outcome-neutral fact has nowhere to go. No rule says that a faction-wide power or protocol is not the unit's own outcome.
proposals.change: Add on_death.notes with this description: "Facts about the death that don't change the outcome: riders killed with the vehicle, weapons left behind for anyone to pick up, a short window to jump out by hand, or a faction-wide power that changes what happens when units die. Such a power is not the unit's own outcome."
proposals.expected: Hammer: [bail-out], proposal, with notes on the protocol that can release a drone. IFV: [bail-out], proposal, with notes that in the source the rider is killed with the car. Riflemen: [respawn], proposal, with notes on dropped weapons. Attack helicopter: [respawn], in-game, with notes on the burning phase when the crew can still jump out. All three coders code the outcomes the same way.
proposals.side_effects: build-docs should show the notes in the samples' On death row. Optional sample enrichment: add these notes to the Hammer and IFV in data/units/ra3.json. The IFV's as_player text already says that both players are thrown out hurt, which matches bail-out. The armament and patterns groups decide separately whether dropped weapons or the protocol need a pattern.

proposals.evidence: armament.mount is 94.4% among coders (a per-unit set measure, which hides per-weapon splits) but contradicts the sample: on the Hammer, all three chose slow-turret and the sample has free-aim (61.1% against the reference). Per-weapon splits: B coded the IFV missiles free-aim where A, C and the sample have body-aim, and C coded the helicopter's TV missile (gunner) body-aim where A and B have free-aim. Hesitations: 10 of 12 reports (A-coh1, A-ra3, A-sc2, A-bf, B-bf, B-ra3, B-sc2, C-bf, C-ra3, C-sc2). Unclear rules: B-ra3 (should a proposed mount follow source facts or playability?), C-bf (no mount for a missile launched along the nose and then steered by the gunner).
proposals.root_cause: The mount is a proposal and nothing ranks the mounts a body allows. hull-turret allows free-aim, slow-turret and auto-target with no preference. Each family's default_aim (free-aim for rockets and cannons) pulls against the physical mount (pods fixed forward, a car with no turret). slow-turret's description says nothing about which turrets are slow. Nothing says a gunner cannot use body-aim, and nothing covers a squad's followers.
proposals.target: data/vocab/aim-models.json: new tie_breaks entry and source_rule on slow-turret and body-aim; schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs weapon.properties.mount.description; scripts/validate.mjs
proposals.change:
tie_breaks: {terms: [radial, auto-target, free-aim, limited-arc, slow-turret, body-aim], rule: "Go down this list and take the first that fits. (1) It hits all around the unit at once, like an aura or a pulse: radial. (2) It is a point-defence or interception system or an automatic sentry, or it launches drones that act on their own: auto-target. (3) A soldier or creature carries it, or it is built into a tiny or small body: free-aim. A squad's weapons all take the leader's mount. (4) The source says or shows that it turns across only part of the circle, such as a side sponson, a door gun, a bow gun or a mech torso that twists only partway: limited-arc. If the source doesn't say how far a turret turns, treat it as a full turret. (5) It sits on a full turret, or on a torso that turns all the way round: slow-turret for the main turret of a large or huge ground vehicle or walker, free-aim for any other turret (a medium tank, a roof gun, a chin gun, any aircraft turret). A gun on the same turret, such as a coaxial gun, takes the turret's mount. (6) It is fixed and fires where the unit faces (no turret, wing pods, forward launchers, bombs): body-aim. If a seat other than the driver fires it, use free-aim instead, because that seat cannot turn the unit. The family's default mount only fills in when the source says nothing about how the weapon is mounted."}
slow-turret source_rule: "The main turret of a large or huge ground vehicle or walker, and any gun on that turret."
body-aim source_rule: "A fixed weapon fired from the driver seat. Never on a gunner, commander or passenger seat."
mount description: "Our proposed mount for a player version, picked from the source's physical mount by the Aim / mount tie-break."
validate.mjs, new error: body-aim on a weapon whose seat is not the driver.
proposals.expected: Hammer: cannon and leech beam slow-turret (large tank, main turret; the beam is part of the turret), stolen weapon has no mount (adaptive). All three coders already have this; the sample changes (see hammer-mount-sample). Siege Tank: both cannons slow-turret, for all three. IFV: missiles body-aim (no turret; the whole car turns), so B changes; passenger weapons free-aim (another seat), for all three. Attack helicopter: pilot rockets, heat-seekers and TOW body-aim, for all three; chin cannon free-aim (an aircraft turret); gunner's guided missile and TV missile free-aim (fixed launcher, gunner seat), so C changes the TV missile. Terror Drone: free-aim (small body), for all. Riflemen: free-aim (soldiers; the followers take the leader's mount), for all.
proposals.side_effects: Cross-group (bodies list): hull-turret and multi-turret do not allow limited-arc, so a tank's hull machine gun (common in Company of Heroes) would need an atypical entry. Consider adding limited-arc to both. fixed-wing allows only body-aim and auto-target, so a bomber's tail gunner (free-aim from rule 6) would be atypical; that is rare. agreement.mjs measures mount as one set per unit, which hid the TV missile split; measuring per weapon would show it. The Soviet flavour already favours slow-turret, which is consistent with the Hammer fix.

proposals.evidence: armament.mount on the Hammer: the reference has free-aim, while A, B and C all have slow-turret (listed in the agreement report under 'where most coders differ from the reference'). The source puts the leech beam and the stolen-weapon port on the turret, and the sample's own as_player text speaks of the turret staying locked on the target.

proposals.evidence: mobility.handling is 88.9%. On the attack helicopter, A and B chose strafe and C chose drift. Hesitations: 7 of 12 reports (A-bf, B-bf, C-bf: strafe or drift for the helicopter; A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3: keep pivot, the default for many legs, or strafe for the Drone; A-sc2: pivot or steer). proposals.root_cause: Each mobility type lists a default_handling, but mobility.handling is called a proposal with no rule on when to leave the default. strafe and drift overlap for a craft that hovers but carries momentum. pivot is the default for many legs, which fits big spider walkers but not a tiny pouncer, so all three coders and the sample left the default for the Drone without a written reason.
proposals.target: data/vocab/handling.json: new tie_breaks entry; schemas/source-unit.schema.json mobility.properties.handling.description; scripts/validate.mjs (warning)
proposals.expected: Attack helicopter: strafe (rotor default; it can hover and slide sideways, and momentum alone doesn't count), so C changes from drift. Terror Drone: strafe (small on many legs), for all three, matching the sample. Siege Tank and Hammer: pivot (tracks default; no source shows they can't turn on the spot). IFV: steer. Riflemen: strafe. Agreement reaches 100% and matches the samples.
proposals.side_effects: docs/vocabularies.md regenerates. In the 28 games: a slow, lumbering small walker would still get strafe (rare). Airships keep drift and jets keep forward-only by default. A hover tank keeps drift even if the source shows it stopping dead, because the rule never changes drift to strafe. That is acceptable, since hover units are meant to slide.

verdicts.reason: I applied it to every pilot unit and file. Riflemen, Terror Drone, Siege Tank and Hammer end with no seat on any weapon or ability, for all three coders (A and C drop 'driver'; the Hammer's 'gunner' becomes an error once it is solo). The IFV keeps passenger-module only on its 18 passenger weapons, which is valid because passengers.kind is passenger-module. The helicopter keeps 'gunner' on the cannon and the gunner missiles, which is valid for driver-gunner, and drops 'driver' from the pilot weapons, flares, jammer and extinguisher. C's passive Multiturret loses its seat under 'a passive ability has no seat'. That leaves one reading, and it matches the published samples, so no sample changes. Validator: the allowed-seat set (the model's seats, plus crew.seats roles, plus passengers.kind) accepts every sample. Cards keep an explicit seat in their own schema, so nothing clashes. In the 28-game scope, a Foxhole light tank or a PlanetSide 2 Sunderer (driver has no gun) just has no weapon without a seat. Squads and remote units never write one. The wording is plain.

On the pilot it works: C's chin cannon moves to secondary, the pilot's rockets are the driver's main weapon, and the IFV is unchanged. Three units in scope still have two readings. (1) Renegade: the crew-models example says the gunner fires the main gun, but alone the driver fires it. 'Write the seat that fires it in the source' then fits both gunner and driver, and the slot rule ('gunner primary only when the driver has no weapon') also splits. (2) PlanetSide 2 Sunderer or Galaxy: the driver has no gun and two or more gun seats do, so every gunner's main gun would be primary. (3) Proposal crews (a Company of Heroes tank once crew-model-rts makes it driver-gunner): 'only a second weapon ... goes to the gunner' is singular and does not say who fires a gun that turns with the main gun. So the turret machine gun could go to either seat, and the hull gun plus a roof gun do not fit 'a second weapon'. The cross-group parts (slot belongs to the armament group, and the x-provenance and docs change) are flagged correctly.
verdicts.revised_change:
Add to weapon.seat, after the seat-leave-out-driver text: "When crew.basis is in-game, write the seat that fires it in the source when every seat is full. A weapon the source hands to a lone driver whenever its own seat is empty (as in Renegade) still belongs to that seat; say in crew.notes that it passes to the driver. When crew.basis is a proposal, follow decision 2A: the driver fires the main weapon and any gun that turns with it. Every other weapon on its own mount that the source fires at the same time as the main weapon goes to the gunner."
Add to weapon.slot: "primary is the main weapon of the driver seat. Another seat's own main gun is secondary. When the driver seat fires nothing with a full crew (a Foxhole light tank, a PlanetSide 2 Sunderer), the main gun of the first gun seat in the source's seat order is primary, and other seats' guns are secondary."
validate.mjs, two new errors on source units: (1) a primary weapon has a seat other than driver while another weapon has no seat (so the driver has a weapon); (2) two primary weapons on different seats.
Cross-group (armament): that group must accept that primary means the driver seat's main weapon, and must say whether a loadout's default option is written as primary (coder A's helicopter). The x-provenance on seat becomes 'proposal unless crew.basis is in-game', and build-docs and the Conventions line in docs/fields.md say so.

verdicts.reason: Pilot check: the Hammer becomes solo (the source says it fires just one weapon at a time), and the Siege Tank (mode swap), Drone (no operator on the field), IFV (passenger replaces the weapon) and Riflemen (squad, in-game) code the same for all three coders. Every published sample holds. Where it breaks: (a) The solo/driver-gunner tie-break is not limited to RTS units. A MechWarrior mech or a Battlefield jet fires several weapons at once from separate mounts, so the tie-break reads driver-gunner for a one-seat shooter unit. (b) 'players operate this unit in the source' is true of every RTS unit too, so it does not separate in-game from proposal. The registry's control field (commanded, piloted or both) gives a test that can be checked. (c) The analyst's own side-effect list counts the RA2 Apocalypse and SC2 Thor as driver-gunner. Both pick their gun by target (ground or air) and fire one at a time, which shows that coders will split whenever the source is silent on firing together. The rule needs a default and a by-target clause. (d) Upgrade weapons (a Generals Overlord gatling add-on, Comanche rocket pods, a CoH roof machine gun) can be read either way. (e) The example 'a machine gun that picks its own targets' clashes with auto-target in mount-order. Every RTS gun picks its own targets. (f) driver-gunner excludes the power-suit body, which the proposal rule does not say. (g) Many CoH, Dawn of War and Wargame tanks become driver-gunner with hull or side guns that are limited-arc, which hull-turret does not allow. The bodies list must change (a forced cross-group change).
verdicts.revised_change:
1. crew.basis enum: ["in-game", "proposal"] (drop "lore"). Description: "in-game = players sit in this unit in the source and its operating seats are copied from there. That happens only for units players drive in a game whose registry control is piloted or both (Battlefield, PlanetSide 2, Foxhole, WARDOGS, Renegade, MechWarrior), not for AI enemies there. It is also in-game when the source moves a group of soldiers or tiny drones as one unit under one order (a squad). proposal = our pick for a player version: every other unit, including every RTS vehicle, aircraft, walker, drone and lone soldier. A crew named only in background text or voice lines changes nothing; mention it in crew.notes. The basis covers the operating seats (model, seats, solo fallback). Passenger seats are always copied from the source."
2. crew.model description: "Who operates the unit. In-game: copy the source's seats. A group the source moves as one unit: squad. Otherwise solo, unless the coding rules on Crew models give driver-gunner or remote."
3. source_rule texts on crew-models:
- solo: "In-game for a unit with one player seat in the source (a MechWarrior mech, a PlanetSide 2 Lightning). The proposal for every unit without player seats unless driver-gunner, squad or remote applies. A crew named in lore or voice lines does not change it."
- driver-gunner: "In-game when the source has a driver seat and a separate gun seat. As a proposal, only for a vehicle, walker, hover or aircraft of medium size or bigger, never a power suit, that fires two weapons at the same time from separate mounts. A separate mount aims on its own: a roof gun, a gun on the front or side of the hull, a second turret. A gun that turns with the main gun is the same mount. These do not count: weapons swapped by a mode or toggle; weapons the source picks by target type (one for ground, one for air), which fire one at a time; weapons added by an upgrade, a passenger or a kill; and point defence that fires by itself. If the source doesn't say whether two weapons fire together, count them as one at a time. The driver keeps the main weapon and the gunner gets the others (decision 2A)."
- driver-gunner-commander: "In-game only, when the source has a separate seat that spots, marks or commands, or a crew seat that only loads, repairs or runs systems. A gunner seat whose loadout swaps its gun for spotting tools is still a gunner. Never proposed for a unit without player seats."
- squad: "In-game when the source moves two or more soldiers or tiny drones as one unit for their whole life, with one order and a shared fate (Company of Heroes or Dawn of War squads). Units bought in pairs that then act alone are solo."
- remote: "Only when the source has a person who stays on the field, outside the machine, while steering it (a soldier who parks to fly a drone). A note in the lore that the machine was once remote-controlled does not count."
4. tie_breaks on crew-models:
{terms: [solo, driver-gunner], rule: "A unit with player seats copies them, however many weapons its one pilot fires. For a unit without player seats, count what the source unit does, not what its text says: two weapons firing at the same time from separate mounts make driver-gunner (its coding rule says what doesn't count); anything else is solo. Faction flavours never decide a source unit's crew; they only weight generated cards."}
{terms: [solo, remote], rule: "Remote only when an operator stays on the field in the source. Otherwise an uncrewed machine is solo."}
5. validate.mjs, new error on source units: crew.basis in-game, in a game whose registry control is commanded, with a model other than squad. Message: "an RTS unit has no player seats; use basis proposal".
Cross-group, forced (bodies list): add limited-arc to the allowed aim-models of hull-turret and multi-turret, because the gunner's hull and side guns this rule creates are limited-arc. Without it, ordinary CoH, Dawn of War and Wargame tanks would all need atypical entries.
Side-effect list corrected: the RA2 Apocalypse and SC2 Thor stay solo (gun picked by target). A CnC3 Mammoth or a Generals Avenger is driver-gunner only if the source shows both weapons firing together.

verdicts.reason: The attack helicopter becomes full-control for all three with nothing left to weigh, which settles A-bf, B-bf and C-bf. But (1) the tie-break's first test, 'if the driver seat has a weapon of its own', fails Renegade. There the main gun belongs to the gunner seat (see seat-and-primary) and the source hands it to a lone driver. The tie-break then says seat-swap, while the kept Renegade example says full-control. (2) Because of the order, auto-gunner is unreachable whenever the driver has a gun. (3) The new needs-crew text ('not even by changing seats') contradicts its own example, the Foxhole engineer who reloads. If a lone Foxhole player can move into the engineer seat (I believe Foxhole lets players change seats), that tank is seat-swap, so the analyst's 'seat-swap or needs-crew, check while researching' leaves two readings. (4) 'Including the main weapon' does not hold for the PlanetSide 2 Liberator, whose heavy gun sits in another seat. Moving the Liberator to full-control is right, but seat-swap then needs a sourced example whose driver has no gun.
verdicts.revised_change:
full-control description: "Alone, the player drives and still fires a weapon: the driver seat's own weapons, or a weapon the source hands to a lone driver. Weapons in other seats either pass to the driver or wait for a teammate; say which in crew notes." Examples: keep Renegade; replace 'Battlefield tanks: the driver has the main gun' with "Battlefield tanks and attack helicopters: the driver keeps the main gun or the rockets, while the second seat's gun waits for a teammate". Move the PlanetSide 2 Liberator here if its pilot's nose gun is confirmed.
seat-swap description: "Alone, the player must change seats to shoot, because no weapon works from the driver seat: drive or shoot, not both." New example after checking the source: "PlanetSide 2: the Sunderer's driver has no gun, so a lone driver hops into a gun seat to fight".
needs-crew description: "Even by changing seats, a lone player can't do a core job, such as firing the main gun, because the source needs two seats working at once." Keep the Foxhole engineer example only if Foxhole stops a lone player from moving into the engineer seat. Otherwise remove it; that tank is seat-swap.
auto-gunner: unchanged.
tie_breaks: {terms: [full-control, seat-swap, needs-crew, auto-gunner], rule: "Ask what one player alone can do, in this order. (1) The source makes empty gun seats fire by themselves: auto-gunner. (2) A lone driver can still fire something, their own weapon or one the source hands over: full-control, even when other seats' guns go quiet. (3) A lone player can reach the guns by changing seats, even slowly: seat-swap. (4) Otherwise: needs-crew. A proposal crew is always full-control (decision 2A)."}

verdicts.reason: Pilot check: Drone [respawn] proposal, Hammer and IFV [bail-out] proposal, Siege Tank [bail-out] proposal, Riflemen [respawn] proposal, helicopter [respawn] in-game. All three coders converge and the samples hold. The new validator check fits remote (uncrewed, so respawn, and remote already excludes bail-out). Where it breaks: (1) 'In a game where players come back after dying' fits ARC Raiders AI machines, because that game is piloted, so one coder writes respawn in-game and another writes proposal. (2) 'Remains can be ... salvaged' fits ARC Raiders parts looted for crafting and Generals GLA salvage crates, which are pickups, not a wreck. (3) The side effects count CoH2 US crews bailing out and Generals veteran pilots as in-game outcomes, but on-death-notes says a faction-wide effect is not the unit's outcome. Both are faction-wide, so the two proposals contradict each other. The veterancy condition also has no rule. (4) 'MechWarrior ejection' is a manual eject, and the pilot does not walk to a new mech. That contradicts the bail-out rule that jumping out by hand does not count, which pilot-eject does not repeat. (5) A Battlefield 2142 text says a burning vehicle's explosion kills nearby soldiers, so a coder may add death-blast to the helicopter unless the rule says which titles count. (6) Tiberian Dawn and Red Alert 1 vehicles drop a survivor only by chance, which gives two readings for bail-out. (7) 'Everyone inside gets out, passengers too' is a design rule placed in a source_rule.
verdicts.revised_change:
on_death.basis description: "in-game = the source shows what happens when this unit dies: a wreck others can work on, a blast that hurts what is near, crew or a pilot getting out on their own, or, for a unit players drive in a game where they come back after dying (registry control piloted or both), the player going back to pick again. proposal = the source shows nothing special, because the unit is simply gone (almost every RTS unit, and AI enemies in shooters). Then code the default from decision 3C: bail-out for a crewed machine that is not infantry, respawn for everything else. When the source shows an outcome, code only that, with basis in-game, and never add the default. An outcome the unit gets on its own counts even when it needs veterancy or happens only by chance; give the condition in on_death.notes. A power or upgrade the player picks or buys for the whole faction does not count."
respawn description: "Nothing is left: the unit is simply gone. In a player version the player goes back to the buy screen (a remote operator goes back to their parked soldier)."
respawn source_rule: "In-game for a unit players drive in a game where they come back after it dies, including a vehicle whose crew die inside it. For a unit that is simply gone in the source, it is the proposal for infantry, organic units and uncrewed machines."
bail-out description, add: "Everyone inside gets out, passengers too."
bail-out source_rule: "In-game when the crew or riders get out on their own as the vehicle dies, even when only one gets out or only by chance. Jumping out by hand before it dies does not count; in our game that is the hold-X key every vehicle has. It is the proposal for any crewed machine outside the infantry class that is simply gone in the source."
wreck source_rule: "In-game only when the remains stay on the field and a unit can repair, recrew or salvage them in the same match. Remains that only block the way or give cover do not count, nor do crates, weapons or loot that drop for pickup or for crafting later; put those in on_death.notes."
death-blast source_rule: "In-game only when the source says the explosion hurts units nearby, for this unit in its own title (for a series, the titles its registry entry leads with). A blast that is only for show, or a wreck that only hurts what it falls on, does not count."
pilot-eject source_rule: "In-game when the pilot leaves the wreck on their own as a unit that can keep fighting, such as walking to a new vehicle or a pickup. Ejecting by hand before the unit dies does not count."
tie_breaks:
{terms: [respawn, bail-out], rule: "A crewed vehicle that is simply gone in the source: bail-out, basis proposal. A vehicle players drive in a shooter whose crew die inside it: respawn, basis in-game, even when they could have jumped out by hand first."}
{terms: [respawn, wreck, death-blast, pilot-eject], rule: "Use two outcomes only when the source shows both, such as a husk that also explodes. Never pair a sourced outcome with the 3C default."}
validate.mjs, two new errors on source units: (1) when basis is proposal, outcomes must be [bail-out] if nature is crewed-machine and class is not infantry, otherwise [respawn]. Message: "a proposal death outcome is the 3C default; if the source shows another outcome, set basis in-game". (2) respawn with basis in-game in a game whose registry control is commanded. Message: "an RTS unit that is simply gone is a proposal".
agreement.mjs measures on_death.basis. Side effects corrected: Generals USA veteran pilots are pilot-eject in-game (condition in notes); CoH2 US crews are bail-out in-game (a built-in faction rule, not a picked power); GLA salvage crates and ARC Raiders loot go to notes; MechWarrior counts only if its pilot leaves on their own and keeps fighting.

verdicts.reason: The field is needed. With it, the Hammer protocol, the IFV rider, the CoH dropped weapons and the Battlefield burning phase each have a home, and all three coders code the same outcomes. But the sentence 'a faction-wide power ... is not the unit's own outcome' catches built-in faction rules that on-death-plain-death counts as in-game outcomes: CoH2 US crews bailing out, and Generals USA veteran pilots. Coders would split on these. The line should run between what the player picks or buys for the faction (an RA3 protocol, a Generals general's upgrade such as the Demo explosions) and what the unit always does. The field also needs a place for crates and loot, and for conditions such as veterancy or chance.
verdicts.revised_change: Add on_death.notes (type string) with this description: "Facts about the death that don't change the outcome: riders killed with the vehicle, a short window to jump out by hand, weapons, crates or loot left for pickup or for crafting, the condition on an outcome (only with veterancy, only by chance), or a power or upgrade the player picks or buys for the whole faction that changes what happens when units die (an RA3 protocol, a Generals general's upgrade). Such a picked power is not the unit's own outcome. A built-in rule that applies to the unit without any pick, such as a faction whose vehicle crews always bail out, is an outcome." build-docs shows on_death.notes in the samples' On death row. Optional: add these notes to the Hammer (protocol) and the IFV (rider killed in the source) in data/units/ra3.json.

verdicts.reason: Pilot check: Hammer and Siege Tank get slow-turret, the IFV missiles body-aim (B changes), the IFV passenger weapons free-aim, the helicopter pilot weapons body-aim and its chin cannon free-aim, and its gunner missiles free-aim (C's TV missile changes). Drone and Riflemen get free-aim. All three coders agree. Where it breaks: (1) The soldier rule (3) comes before limited-arc (4). A Company of Heroes machine-gun team or anti-tank gun crew therefore gets free-aim, which loses its defining fixed arc, the thing flankers use. (2) A tank destroyer (a CoH StuG) whose gun turns a few degrees fits both (4) limited-arc and (6) fixed body-aim. (3) 'Large or huge ground vehicle or walker' leaves hover-class tanks unclear, since their class is hover but their target type is ground-vehicle. (4) 'An automatic sentry' could take in a unit the player controls, such as a Generals Sentry Drone. (5) Jargon: coaxial, sponson, bow gun. (6) The validator error should also cover example cards. A bomber's tail gun is limited-arc under (4), not free-aim as the side effects say. The bodies change (limited-arc on hull-turret, multi-turret and humanoid) is forced, not optional: under 4B a hull gun or a set-up machine gun is not physical nonsense.

tie_breaks on aim-models: {terms: [radial, auto-target, limited-arc, free-aim, slow-turret, body-aim], rule: "Go down this list and take the first that fits. (1) It hits all around the unit at once, like an aura or a pulse: radial. (2) It fires by itself while the unit's player does something else (point defence, interceptors, a deployed sentry gun, or launched drones that act on their own): auto-target. (3) The source shows it covering only part of the circle: a gun on the side or front of a hull, a door gun, a tail gun, a mech torso that twists only partway, or a soldiers' heavy weapon that must be set up and then covers only an arc (a machine-gun team, a field gun): limited-arc. (4) A soldier or creature carries it, or it is built into a tiny or small body: free-aim. A squad's weapons all take the leader's mount. verdicts.reason: It holds under the revised mount-order. Pilot check: helicopter strafe (C changes from drift), Drone strafe (small or tiny on many legs), Siege Tank and Hammer pivot, IFV steer, Riflemen strafe. The coders converge and match the samples, which settles A-bf, B-bf, C-bf, A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3 and A-sc2. Where it breaks: the PlanetSide 2 Magrider, a hover tank whose strafing the registry notes name as a pattern to record, stays drift, because the rule only takes ability away from the default. In a game where players drive the unit, handling is a source fact, so a hover tank that strafes would be coded badly. Allowing the reverse change everywhere would be wrong: RTS engines turn wheeled models on the spot, which would flip many wheeled units to pivot. So the reverse change must be limited to piloted games and to sideways movement. The proposed warning fires on every changed unit, even one that already gives its reason, so it adds noise. It should fire only when mobility.notes is empty. Modes with their own mobility are not covered.
verdicts.revised_change:
tie_breaks on handling: {terms: [strafe, pivot, steer, drift, forward-only], rule: "Start from the default handling of the unit's mobility type. Change it only for one of these reasons, and name the reason in mobility.notes. (1) A tiny or small unit on legs (two legs or many) gets strafe. (2) The source clearly shows the unit can't do what the default needs: if it can't turn on the spot, pivot becomes steer; if it can't stop or hover, strafe becomes forward-only; if it can't stop quickly and only slides through turns, with no hover and no sideways move, strafe becomes drift. (3) In a game where players drive the unit (registry control piloted or both), the source clearly shows it sliding sideways at will, such as a hover tank built to strafe: strafe. Momentum, tilting to speed up, a heavy feel, or an RTS model turning on the spot never change it on their own; put them in mobility.notes. A mode with its own mobility type follows the same rule from that type."}
handling description: "Our proposal for how a player version would handle. Use the mobility type's default unless the Handling tie-break gives a reason to change it; write the reason in mobility.notes."
validate.mjs, new warning on source units: handling differs from the mobility default, the unit is not tiny or small on legs, and mobility.notes is empty. Message: "say why the handling differs in mobility.notes".
Expected in scope: PlanetSide 2 Magrider strafe; RTS hover units keep drift; jets keep forward-only.

The boost wording is right: Riflemen get no boost from all three coders. But the two-way validator error can leave a unit with no valid coding. The analyst says that if the abilities group keeps dash on retreat, all three must add boost, yet the new boost text forbids boost for retreat. The data would then fail whatever the coder writes. The reverse check also catches abilities that are not on a key (SC2 Zealot Charge fires by itself; coded as a triggered ability linking dash, it would force a key-bound trait), and it ignores modes whose 'via' links the pattern. The Siege Tank (deploy-anchor plus a deploy ability) and the samples (amphibious and crush need no key) pass either way.
verdicts.revised_change:
